reason: The pointwise limit is identified explicitly, and a fixed ε witnesses failure of the uniform convergence quantifiers.
text:
For each x∈[0,1), we have x^n→0, while f_n(1)=1 for every n. Thus the pointwise limit is

f(x)={0 if 0≤x<1, 1 if x=1}.

If (f_n) converged uniformly, its uniform limit would necessarily equal this pointwise limit f. Fix ε=1/2. For every N∈Z_+, choose n=N and x=2^{-1/N}∈[0,1). Then f(x)=0 and

|f_n(x)−f(x)|=x^N=1/2.

Hence, for every N, there exist n≥N and x∈[0,1] such that |f_n(x)−f(x)|≥ε. This contradicts the criterion for uniform convergence. Therefore (f_n) does not converge uniformly on [0,1].
